facts.statement: Anteophthalmosuchus is an extinct genus of goniopholidid neosuchian that lived during the Early Cretaceous in southern England, eastern Spain, and western Belgium.
facts.quote: Anteophthalmosuchus (meaning "forward-pointing eye crocodile") is an extinct genus of goniopholidid neosuchian from the Early Cretaceous of southern England, eastern Spain, and western Belgium.

facts.statement: Anteophthalmosuchus measured approximately 3.5 to 4 meters in length with a skull length of about 60 centimeters.
facts.quote: It measured around 3.5–4 m in length, and had a skull length of about 60 cm.

facts.statement: The holotype of Anteophthalmosuchus is a well-preserved skull and partial skeleton found in the Wealden Group of the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Anteophthalmosuchus, from the Wealden Group of the Isle of Wight, includes a well-preserved skull and partial skeleton.

facts.statement: Hooley's specimen was redescribed as the distinct genus and species Anteophthalmosuchus hooleyi in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, Hooley's specimen was redescribed as a distinct genus and species of goniopholidid called Anteophthalmosuchus hooleyi.

facts.statement: A. hooleyi is distinguished from Goniopholis crassidens by the lack of a mandibular fenestra, very wide supratemporal fenestrae, and a small palpebral bone that does not extend over the eye socket.
facts.quote: Features that distinguish A. hooleyi from Goniopholis crassidens include the lack of a hole in the lower jaw called the mandibular fenestra, very wide supratemporal fenestrae (openings) on the skull table, and a bone above the eye socket called the palpebral that is small and does not extend over the socket as in some other goniopholidids.

facts.statement: Two specimens from Bernissart, Belgium, known as "Dollo's goniopholidid", were referred to A. hooleyi in a 2016 redescription.
facts.quote: Two specimens from Bernissart, Belgium, collectively referred to as "Dollo's goniopholidid", was referred to A. hooleyi in a 2016 redescription.

facts.statement: A. escuchae is known solely from the holotype AR-1-1097, which consists of a partial skull.
facts.quote: It is known solely from the holotype AR-1-1097 which consists of a partial skull.

facts.statement: A. escuchae was collected from the early Albian-aged Escucha Formation at the Santa Maria Mine in Ariño, Teruel Province, Aragon.
facts.quote: It was collected from the early Albian-aged Escucha Formation, at Santa Maria Mine located in the municipality of Ariño, Teruel Province, of Aragon, along with the closely related Hulkepholis plotos.

facts.statement: A. hooleyi lacked an external mandibular fenestra, a trait shared with G. baryglyphaeus but not G. crassidens.
facts.quote: Unlike Goniopholis crassidens, but like G. baryglyphaeus (and another specimen, IRSNB R1537), A. hooleyi lacked an external mandibular fenestra (the opening situated posteriorly, or towards the back of, the mandible).

facts.statement: Anteophthalmosuchus is classified as a mesoeucrocodylian goniopholidid within the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: superordo: Crocodylomorpha ordo: Mesoeucrocodylia familia: Goniopholididae genus: Anteophthalmosuchus

facts.statement: Anteophthalmosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous in southern England, eastern Spain, and western Belgium.
facts.quote: Anteophthalmosuchus (nombre que significa "cocodrilo con ojos que apuntan hacia adelante") es un género extinto de mesoeucrocodilio goniofolídido del Cretácico Inferior del sur de Inglaterra, el este de España, y el oeste de Bélgica.

facts.statement: Anteophthalmosuchus was included in a phylogenetic analysis of goniopholidids before its specimen was redescribed.
facts.quote: Anteophthalmosuchus hooleyi fue incluido en un análisis filogenético de los goniofolídidos que fue publicado un poco antes de que el espécimen fuera redescrito.

facts.statement: Specimens of Anteophthalmosuchus were found to be the closest relatives of a specimen known as the "Hulke goniopholid", now called Hulkepholis willetti.
facts.quote: Se descubrió que los especímenes de Hooley y Dollo eran los parientes más cercanos de un espécimen conocido como el "goniofolídido de Hulke", ahora conocido como Hulkepholis willetti.

facts.statement: The parent group of Anteophthalmosuchus is Goniopholididae.
Anteophthalmosuchus is classified as a reptile.
The type species of the genus Anteophthalmosuchus is Anteophthalmosuchus hooleyi.
Anteophthalmosuchus lived from the Hauterivian to the Albian stages, between 132.6 and 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Albian (132.6 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 10 recorded fossil occurrences of Anteophthalmosuchus.
